description:
pkix-revocation/src/signer_discovery.rs:14-26 and the new_with_signer_discovery rustdoc commit to: discovery walks the bundle structurally (AKI/SKI/DN), checks cRLSign in KeyUsage, and checks structural reachability to a self-signed cert — but verifies NO signatures along the way.

This is correct and worth defending. Pulling pkix-path::validate_path into the discovery constructor would invert the workspace's one-way dependency direction (AGENTS.md non-negotiable #2: 'pkix-path is no_std; pkix-revocation depends on pkix-path; no reverse'). A future contributor who sees the 'lenient' comment and thinks 'we should make this strict by validating the signer's chain in-process' would force pkix-revocation to depend on the full path validator — a structural regression.

The correct strict-validation path is composing this with pkix-chain (or any caller that has already validated the bundle). The lenient/strict tradeoff is tracked separately as PKIX-yi7k.1. Do not change this without revisiting the dependency direction.

What a future contributor might incorrectly suggest:
- 'reaches_self_signed should verify signatures' → would invert deps
- 'discover_crl_signer should call full path validation' → same
- 'new_with_signer_discovery should accept a SignatureVerifier and use it on the chain' → same (the SignatureVerifier we have is for the CRL itself; reusing it to validate the bundle chain bypasses the rest of §6.1)
title: Discovery is structural-only; signature verification deferred to pkix-chain
